text:
Ava: quick follow-up from the pricing segment — wanted to clear up a few common questions we saw about credits, rate caps, and burst behavior. ask here and we’ll answer.
Rohit: thanks, ava. first q: is there a hard global rate cap for free-tier accounts or just per-route quotas?
Ava: short answer: per-route quotas + soft burst windows. we do have protective global limits to stop abuse but they’re very high and rarely hit. the user-visible limits are per-route.
Maya: to add — credits themselves are usage units and don’t change route-level caps. you can run out of credits but still be blocked by rate limits if you exceed per-second quotas.
Liam: can we get specifics? e.g., what happens when you exceed a per-route rate? 429s or queued?
Rohit: behavior depends on route config. defaults: requests over quota get 429 with Retry-After. Dedicated customers can opt into short queuing (5s) or fallback routing to cheaper model variants.
Sofia: a customer asked about automated backoff recommendations — will the SDK surface Retry-After or exponential backoff guidance?
Kenji: SDKs return the Retry-After header and emit an event in the client: 'rate_limit.hit'. we plan to add a helper that implements jittered exp backoff and token-bucket friendly retry for 2026-01.
Ava: we’ll publish a short KB with recommended backoff patterns and sample code by EOD tomorrow.
Rohit: question about credits replenishment: if a workspace has monthly credits and we top up mid-month, do unused credits roll into next month?
Maya: currently no roll-over for promotional credits. committed credits (reserved capacity) follow contract terms and are billed monthly; any roll-over is contract-specific. we’re evaluating a small rollover pilot for enterprise.
Liam: what about credit expiration for free trial credits?
Maya: free trial credits expire 90 days after issuance. there’s an automated reminder at 30 days.
Sofia: customer reported credits draining fast because of streaming tokens + tool calls. are tool calls billed differently?
Rohit: tool/function-calling currently counts generated tokens + tool output tokens. we’re working on a metering change to bill tool-call orchestration separately in 2H roadmap — will be opt-in initially.
Kenji: small ops note — health-check endpoints are exempt from billing but still counted against a very small health-check rate quota. this prevents noise without letting health-check loops bypass protections.
Ava: good callout. for enterprise customers we can create custom exemptions (e.g., infra health-checks) as part of Private/Dedicated onboarding.
Rohit: about graceburst/overage — if a user exceeds monthly committed credits, do we auto-charge for overage or throttle?
Maya: for Reserved customers we prefer overage billing by default with alerts at 80/90/100%. For self-serve accounts we have a soft-fallback: temporary soft-throttle + email alert, then automatic block if they hit a hard safety threshold.
Sofia: request from support — can we get a single view in Console showing per-route consumption vs credits remaining for quick triage?
Liam: Console already has token-level breakdown for calls per model and per-route; we’ll add a "credits remaining" overlay in the next UI sprint.
Ava: roadmap note: next quarter we’ll ship per-route burst profiles (low/medium/high) so teams can tune latency vs cost in Console.
Rohit: any exemptions for internal developer sandboxes?
Kenji: internal sandboxes are on an org tier that has a higher soft cap and uses a separate dev-credit pool. it’s not visible to customers.
Sofia: another customer question — if they have both Hosted and Dedicated in a hybrid setup, do credits mix?
Maya: Hosted credits do not apply to Dedicated usage. Dedicated is contract-based capacity; Hosted credits are for the public API only. we can map billing to a single invoice but units remain separate.
Rohit: quick policy clarification: can teams request temporary credit grants for demo days? process?
Maya: yes — Support handles one-off grants. include expected duration, volume estimate, and demo date. approvals usually same-day for internal sales demos.
Ava: thanks everyone. action items: (1) maya & rohit — publish KB + FAQ by EOD tomorrow, (2) liam & kenji — confirm SDK backoff helper timeline in eng-sprint notes, (3) product will draft a short Console mock for credits overlay.

Rohit: i’ll ping when the KB is live. feel free to drop more follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
